_comment: Hand-maintained (unlike openapi.json, WS payloads have no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI export in trading-platform2). For each private/public WS event type the app parses, `keys` lists every JSON key the backend actually puts in the envelope's `data` object across ALL call sites (union — a given message may carry a subset). Update this file by re-reading the cited backend source whenever a WS payload changes; DtoContractTest's WS test asserts the keys the app reads (hard-coded there, mirroring WsRepository.kt / PrivateWsClient.kt / PublicWsClient.kt) are a subset of the matching event's `keys` here.

portfolio_update.source: trading-platform2 app/portfolio/consumer.py:2151-2162 (ws_payload, built in _record_order_execution) -> app/websocket/private_handler.py:37-38 send_portfolio_update
portfolio_update.notes: No daily_pnl/total_pnl/nav key is ever sent on this channel — it is an order-execution snapshot, not a NAV/P&L tick. Matches the KDoc on WsRepository.portfolioUpdates (data/repository/WsRepository.kt:29-38).

position_update.source: trading-platform2 app/portfolio/consumer.py:2170-2200 (ws_position_payload, built in _record_order_execution) -> app/websocket/private_handler.py:40-41 send_position_update
position_update.notes: No position_id key is ever sent — matches the KDoc on WsRepository.positionUpdates (data/repository/WsRepository.kt:57-66). `current_price` (the app's fallback name for `last_price`) is likewise never sent by any current call site.

order_update.source: trading-platform2 app/execution/consumer.py:91-112 (_send_order_ws_update base fields + extra=) and app/execution/exit_consumer.py:1108-1131,1219-1233 (same helper, exit-order call sites)
order_update.notes: PR-5c FINDING (new, not previously tracked in audit/PLAN.md): no call site of _send_order_ws_update ever sets a `fill_price` key — only `price` (the requested/limit price at SUBMITTED time). WsRepository.orderUpdates reads `fill_price` (data/repository/WsRepository.kt:102), which is therefore always null. See PR report.

notification.notes: PR-5c FINDING (new): the backend key is `notification_type`, never `type`. PrivateWsClient.kt:445 reads `data.optString("type", "info")`, which therefore always falls back to the "info" default. PrivateWsClient.kt:447 also falls back to a `message` key for `body` (`data.optString("body", data.optString("message", ""))`) that no call site ever sends either — harmless since `body` itself is always sent, but dead code, and undocumented (no KDoc, unlike the position_update `current_price` fallback). See PR report.

strategy_signal.notes: confidence is sent as a numeric STRING (str(result.confidence)); org.json's JSONObject.optDouble() coerces numeric strings via Double.parseDouble, so WsRepository.strategySignals' optDoubleOrNull("confidence") decodes it correctly — not a drift.

catalyst_event.notes: PR-5c FINDING (new): the backend key is `catalyst_type`, never `event_type`; there is no top-level `title`/`description` — those would have to come from inside the nested `data` (event_data) object, which WsRepository does not descend into. WsRepository.catalystEvents reads `event_type`/`title`/`description` (data/repository/WsRepository.kt:123-126), which are therefore always null. See PR report.

market_data.envelope: {"type": "market_data", "data": {...}, "timestamp": "..."} (public /ws/public channel, distinct from the private channel above)
market_data.notes: PR-5c FINDING (new): only `symbol`/`price` are unconditionally present; open/high/low/close/volume/bid/ask/source/data_mode are each included only `if val is not None`. The public bridge NEVER sends `source_name`, `source_type` or `quality` (those three appear only on the separate admin_events.py channel, app/websocket/admin_events.py:166-167) — PublicWsClient.parseMarketData reads all three (data/websocket/PublicWsClient.kt:143-147) and they are therefore always null on this channel. Also note the key sent is `source` (singular free-text), not `source_name`/`source_type`. See PR report.
